title: Cold rebuild: Standup
summary: Rebuild sk standup from memory: three LINQ queries over your tasks and time entries.

steps.title: Rebuild it from memory
body: Before the boss, prove that **Standup** survived. This step is a *cold rebuild*:
- the editor starts **empty**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at;
- the tests are **exactly** the ones your Sidekick piece passed;
- it is short: one piece, from the spec alone.
Why: pulling something out of memory (instead of re-reading it) is what makes it stick. If you get stuck, that is
useful information, not failure: go back to the lesson, then come back here tomorrow.

steps.prompt: `today` is Monday 30 November 2026. What does this print?
steps.explain: On a Monday the standup's "yesterday" is the previous workday: Friday.

steps.title: Cold: Standup
prompt: Write, from memory, `static string Standup(IEnumerable<TaskItem> tasks, IEnumerable<TimeEntry> entries, DateOnly today)`:
- Yesterday = `Sk.PreviousWorkday(today)` as `ddd d MMM`; every task with entries that day, in task order, minutes
- Today: open tasks not tagged `blocked`, `Sk.PriorityScore` highest first, then `Id`, at most 3; none: `- nothing planned`.
- Blockers: open tasks tagged `blocked`; none: `- none`. Lines joined with `\n`, no trailing newline.
solution: static string Standup(IEnumerable<TaskItem> tasks, IEnumerable<TimeEntry> entries, DateOnly today)
var lines = new List<string> { $"Yesterday ({yesterday:ddd d MMM}):" };
lines.AddRange(worked.Any() ? worked : new List<string> { "- nothing logged" });
lines.AddRange(next.Any() ? next : new List<string> { "- nothing planned" });
template: DateTime DojoAt(int day, int h, int m) => new DateTime(2026, 11, day, h, m, 0);
new(1, "Fix login redirect", 45) { Tag = "bug", Due = dojoToday },
Dojo.Eq("line 1 names the previous workday", "Yesterday (Tue 24 Nov):", dojoReport.ElementAtOrDefault(0));
Dojo.Eq("time is summed per task, in task order", "- Fix login redirect (1h 30m)", dojoReport.ElementAtOrDefault(1));
Dojo.Eq("finished tasks you worked on count too", "- Review Ana's pull request (0h 25m)", dojoReport.ElementAtOrDefault(2));
Dojo.Eq("today: highest priority first", "- Fix login redirect", dojoReport.ElementAtOrDefault(4));
Dojo.Eq("today: then the rest by priority, then id", "- Write parser tests", dojoReport.ElementAtOrDefault(5));
Dojo.Eq("today: at most three", "- Upgrade to .NET 10", dojoReport.ElementAtOrDefault(6));
Dojo.Eq("blocked tasks are blockers, not plans", "- Waiting on API keys", dojoReport.ElementAtOrDefault(8));
var dojoMonday = Standup(dojoTasks, dojoEntries, new DateOnly(2026, 11, 30)).Split('\n');
Dojo.Eq("on a Monday, yesterday is Friday", "Yesterday (Fri 27 Nov):", dojoMonday.ElementAtOrDefault(0));
Dojo.Eq("nothing logged says so", "- nothing logged", dojoMonday.ElementAtOrDefault(1));
var dojoEmpty = Standup(new List<TaskItem>(), new List<TimeEntry>(), dojoToday);

Dojo.Eq("an empty Sidekick", "Yesterday (Tue 24 Nov):
- nothing logged
Today:
- nothing planned
Blockers:
- none", dojoEmpty);
internal static DateOnly PreviousWorkday(DateOnly day) => day.DayOfWeek switch
internal static DateOnly WeekStart(DateOnly day) => day.AddDays(-(((int)day.DayOfWeek + 6) % 7));
internal static string Ago(DateTime then, DateTime now)
internal static int PriorityScore(TaskItem task, DateOnly today)
internal static List<TaskItem> TopPriorities(IEnumerable<TaskItem> tasks, DateOnly today, int count)
return open.Count <= count ? open : open.GetRange(0, count);
public TaskItem(int id, string title, int estimateMinutes = 0)
if (id < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(id), "Task ids start at 1.");
if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(title)) throw new ArgumentException("A task needs a title.", nameof(title));
if (estimateMinutes < 0) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(estimateMinutes), "An estimate cannot be negative.");
public int LoggedMinutes { get; private set; }
public bool IsRunning { get; private set; }
public DateTime StartedAt { get; private set; }
public bool Done { get; private set; }
string projectPart = Project is { Length: > 0 } p ? $" @{p}" : "";
string duePart = Due is DateOnly d ? $" (due {d:ddd d MMM})" : "";
if (Done) throw new InvalidOperationException("A finished task cannot be started.");
if (at < StartedAt) throw new ArgumentException("A timer cannot stop before it started.", nameof(at));
if (minutes < 1) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(minutes), "Log at least one minute.");
enum Status { Todo, Doing, Blocked, Done }
record TimeEntry(int TaskId, DateTime Start, DateTime End)
public static bool CanMove(Status from, Status to) => (from, to) switch
(Status.Doing, Status.Todo or Status.Blocked or Status.Done) => true,
steps.explain: Three small queries, each a sentence: tasks with entries yesterday, open unblocked tasks by priority, blocked tasks. It reuses four pieces you wrote in earlier modules; if one of them were wrong, your standup would be wrong too.
